title: AiEvalReview
wrapsNative: NavigationSplitView(sidebar:detail:) with List(selection:) for the queue and a ScrollView for the item (a navigation stack on iPhone); Picker with .pickerStyle(.segmented) for the verdict; ProgressView with .progressViewStyle(.monarchLinear); TextField(axis: .vertical) in MonarchFormField for notes
summary: A recipe, not a component: a review queue for AI outputs, with each output's prompt, output and expected answer, a 1 to 5 rubric per criterion, notes and a pass or fail verdict.
whenToUse: Human evaluation of model or prompt changes, or spot-checking AI outputs before a feature launches or a model is switched.
whenNotToUse: For end-user feedback on one reply use MonarchAiFeedback. For reviewing AI drafts before they are sent use MonarchAiDraftQueue.
api: NavigationSplitView(sidebar: { List(selection: $current) { ProgressView("N of M reviewed", value:, total:).progressViewStyle(.monarchLinear); ForEach(items) { VStack { Text(title); Text(verdict) }.tag(item.id) } } }, detail: { ScrollView { … } })
MonarchRatingPicker(criterion.label, value: score(item.id, criterion.id), in: 1...criterion.scale, isClearable: true)
Picker("Verdict", selection: verdict(item.id)) { Text("Pass").tag("pass" as String?); Text("Fail").tag("fail" as String?) }.pickerStyle(.segmented)
MonarchButton("Previous" / "Next", size: .sm) { … }.disabled(…); MonarchButton("Submit reviews", variant: .primary, fullWidth: true) { … }

options.name: items
options.type: App list of outputs: id, title, prompt, output, reference
options.description: The queue. The output is Markdown text for MonarchAiMarkdown; the reference is optional and its block is left out without it.

options.name: rubric
options.type: App list of criteria: id, label, detail, scale
options.description: One MonarchRatingPicker per criterion, scored 1 to scale (at most 5), with its detail as a caption above it.

options.name: reviews
options.type: Scores, notes and verdict per item id (app state)
options.description: Held by the app and persisted on every change, as the web's onReviewChange.

options.name: current
options.description: The item shown in the detail column; Previous and Next change it, and selecting a row pushes it on iPhone.

options.name: advance on verdict
options.description: Set current to the next item in the verdict binding's setter to move on after pass or fail, as the web's advanceOnVerdict.

states.name: pending
states.description: A queue row reads "Not reviewed" under its title.

states.name: pass / fail
states.description: The row reads "Pass" or "Fail", and the segmented picker shows the selected segment.

states.name: current
states.description: The queue row of the item shown is the List selection, highlighted by the system and read as selected.

states.name: scored
states.description: "Score 9 / 13" sums the scores given; each picker reads its value.

states.name: first / last
states.description: Previous is disabled on the first item, Next on the last.

states.name: done
states.description: The progress bar is full and Submit reviews is enabled once every item has a verdict.

states.name: empty
states.description: With no item selected or no items, the detail shows a MonarchEmptyState.

appearance: Every part is an existing control: the system list and segmented picker in the Monarch theme, the linear MonarchProgressViewStyle, MonarchAiGeneratedBadge on the AI roles, MonarchAiMarkdown, MonarchRatingPicker, MonarchFormField and small MonarchButtons. Light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow from those components.
platformNotes: The web ships AiEvalReview as one component with a sticky queue column beside the item from 768px and the queue stacked above it below. On iOS it is a recipe on the list-detail pattern, as on Android (NavigableListDetailPaneScaffold): NavigationSplitView shows the queue and the item side by side on iPad and in landscape on large iPhones, and collapses to a navigation stack on iPhone, where selecting a row pushes the item and the system back gesture returns to the queue. The web's radio choices per criterion are MonarchRatingPicker; its pass and fail radios are a segmented Picker (Android: a single-choice segmented button row). The web's J / K and P / F shortcuts and the visible shortcut hint are left out: the web hides the hint on touch screens, and an app that wants them for hardware keyboards adds .keyboardShortcut to Previous and Next or .onKeyPress on the detail. The web moves focus to the new item's heading after Previous and Next; this recipe does not move focus. The web's check, cross and dot glyphs in the queue are left out; the verdict is the row's second line of text, as on Android.
accessibility: Each queue row is one element (title and verdict combined) in a List with selection, so VoiceOver reads its title, its verdict as text and whether it is selected.
The Prompt, Output, Expected, Rubric and Verdict labels are headers, so the VoiceOver rotor moves between them; the item's title is the navigation title.
The output carries MonarchAiGeneratedBadge, read as AI-generated.
Each MonarchRatingPicker is named by its criterion and reads its value, for example "3 of 5".
Pass and Fail are a system segmented Picker: VoiceOver reads the picker's label, each segment and the selected state, not colour alone.
Previous, Next and Submit reviews are MonarchButtons with 44-point targets, read as dimmed when disabled.
edgeCases: Keep each criterion at five points or fewer, as the web does.
Persist every change; nothing in the recipe saves reviews by itself.
Do not show which model produced an output when reviewers should judge blind.
A long output scrolls in the detail; the queue scrolls on its own, so do not put the split view in a scrolling parent.
Clearing a score (isClearable) removes it from the total.
